value.rationale: A single natural nonautonomous open-doubling family has explicitly evaluable and mathematically different dynamical phases: an infinite countable heteroclinic survivor and a Jordan n*2^{-n} escape law; a singleton survivor and pure 2^{-n} tail; and complete extinction after exactly two opportunities. The distinctions are not detected by the constant escape exponent log 2 across the first two regimes. Thresholds occur when actual inverse-branch intervals collide, making them intrinsic rather than selected slices. These explicit benchmarks illuminate the information lost by asymptotic escape-rate approximations and permit testing periodic-hole transfer methods.
